test_title: PYST 34: SSC CHSL 2023 - Quantitative Aptitude(Held On: 14 Aug, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A man borrowed a certain sum of money at the rate of 10% per annum simple interest for the first three years and 15% per annum simple interest for the period beyond three years. If he pays a total interest of Rs. 2884.50 at the end of 7 years, then the sum of money (in Rs.) that he borrowed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Interest % = (Rate₁ × Time₁) + (Rate₂ × Time₂)

Total Interest % = (10% × 3) + (15% × (7 − 3)) = 30% + 60% = 90%

Given: 90% of Sum = ₹2884.50

Sum (100%) = (2884.50 ÷ 90) × 100 = 32.05 × 100 = ₹3205

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3205.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First rate (R₁) = 10%, Time (T₁) = 3 years

Second rate (R₂) = 15%, Time (T₂) = 7 − 3 = 4 years

Total Interest = ₹2884.50

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• Start 3 yrs 7 yrs 10% p.a. 15% p.a. Interest₁ = 30% of P Interest₂ = 60% of P Total Interest (90%) = ₹2884.50

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the borrowed sum be P.

⇒ SI for first 3 years = (P × 10 × 3) ÷ 100 = 30P ÷ 100

⇒ SI for next 4 years = (P × 15 × 4) ÷ 100 = 60P ÷ 100

⇒ Total SI = (30P ÷ 100) + (60P ÷ 100) = 90P ÷ 100

⇒ 90P ÷ 100 = 2884.50

⇒ 0.9P = 2884.50

⇒ P = 2884.50 ÷ 0.9

⇒ P = 28845 ÷ 9 = 3205

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3205.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Variable Rate Simple Interest

When interest rates change over time, the total interest is the sum of interest for each period: Total SI = P × (R₁T₁ + R₂T₂ + R₃T₃ + ...) ÷ 100.

Principal and Amount Relationship

The total amount (A) is the sum of the Principal (P) and the Total Simple Interest (SI): A = P + SI.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.
